openingCue: Jordan’s friend suggests graphic design based on drawing and group work. Which question from alis’s exploration steps would help Jordan investigate before choosing a pathway?
teachingCue: Find an alis exploration step that helps turn an interest, skill, or work value into a question to investigate. Apply it to one of Jordan’s clues.
modelCue: Use one step from the alis page to add a research question to Jordan’s evidence card; keep the question separate from what the supplied observations prove.
practiceCue: Return to alis and select one exploration question that could test whether an occupation’s actual duties fit Jordan’s interest or work value.
limitCue: The exploration steps cannot establish that graphic design fits Jordan or will lead to a job. Check current occupation profiles and local postings for duties, conditions, and entry routes.

openingCue: Leah is weighing an apprenticeship route against a school route. What program or route detail from alis would help her compare them for the same destination?

modelCue: Add one alis route detail to Leah’s fictional route sketch, then label whether it is a confirmed fact or a question to verify with the provider.
practiceCue: Return to alis and choose one route-comparison question that the fictional cost figures cannot answer.
limitCue: The alis overview cannot confirm Leah’s admission, credential, or timetable. Check current institution and regulator pages, then confirm course sequencing with the school.

openingCue: Database Analyst — alis reports a Hot three-year Alberta forecast, while a search near Noor’s home finds two openings. Which details show that the provincial forecast and local search answer different questions?
teachingCue: In Employment & Advancement, record 3-Year Forecast: Hot, Employed in AB: 2,470, Source: 2024–2026 Alberta Short-Term Employment Forecast, and the section update date. Also record the note that some data applies to a broader NOC group.
modelCue: Use the dated Employment & Advancement figures to replace one fictional record, then explain which Alberta question the figures answer and which local question they do not.
practiceCue: Return to Employment & Advancement and identify the forecast measure, Alberta scope, source period, and NOC-group limitation before deciding whether the claim applies to Noor’s town.
limitCue: Database Analyst — alis reports an Alberta forecast for an occupational group. It cannot confirm a local opening, one employer’s requirements, or whether Noor will be hired.

openingCue: Rowan has organized a welcome table and explained a process to helpers. Which Skills for Success category could help Rowan describe one of those actions accurately?

openingCue: Rowan’s first-shift brief says some work must wait for training. Which CCOHS worker right helps Rowan identify what to ask before handling the cleaning spray?

sourceTitle: Skills for Success — Government of Canada

openingCue: Devin is asked to use an unlabelled liquid near a poorly ventilated area. Which worker right from CCOHS is relevant before Devin proceeds?

openingCue: A worker notices that a machine inspection is missing from the closing checklist. Which Alberta OHS page detail could help the worker identify a responsible next step?

modelCue: Use one source detail to turn the vague concern in the worked example into an observable report and a request for follow-up.
practiceCue: Return to Alberta OHS guidance and identify which responsibility or reporting route is relevant to the missed-break practice case.
limitCue: The overview cannot determine from this scenario alone whether a legal duty was breached. Check current legislation and workplace procedures, and seek the appropriate OHS route for unresolved concerns.
